back: The Customs Parliament of 1867 in which the south German states sent deputies to a common body with the North German Confederation.
A report of 13 July 1870 of the king's meeting with the French ambassador, which Bismarck edited to look like an insult.

front: When and where was the German Empire proclaimed?
back: 18 January 1871 in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles; Wilhelm I became German Emperor.
On 1-2 September 1870 the main French army and Napoleon III surrendered; the Second Empire fell on 4 September.

front: What were the terms of the Treaty of Frankfurt (10 May 1871)?
back: France gave up Alsace and part of Lorraine and paid five billion francs in indemnity.

front: How was the Luxemburg crisis of 1867 settled?
back: By the London Conference of May 1867, which neutralised Luxemburg; the Prussian garrison left.

front: Why was Bismarck in a strong position in 1870?
back: France had no allies, its army was weaker and worse led, and the Prussian army and railways were ready.

front: How did the 1871 constitution preserve Prussian dominance?
back: The Emperor was the King of Prussia, controlled the army and appointed the Chancellor; Prussia could block change in the Bundesrat.

front: Did Bismarck plan the war of 1870?
back: Historians disagree: he encouraged the candidature and edited the telegram, but France chose to demand more and declare war.
